chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Urama, from the one who narrated it, from Al-Sadiq, Abu al-Hasan the third (peace be upon him), who said:

You should say: Peace be upon you, O Guardian of Allah! You are the first oppressed one, and the first one whose right was usurped. You were patient and reckoned [your reward] until the certainty (death) came to you. So I testify that you met Allah, and you were a martyr. May Allah punish your murderer with various types of punishment and renew the punishment upon him.

I have come to you recognizing your right, perceiving your affair, and being an enemy to your enemies and those who oppressed you. I shall meet my Lord with that, if Allah wills. O Guardian of Allah! Indeed, I have many sins, so intercede for me to your Lord, for indeed you have a praiseworthy and well-known status with Allah, and indeed you have prestige and intercession with Allah. And the Exalted has said: 'And they will not intercede except for the one whom He approves of.'
Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan the third (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.وَ لا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضى: And they will not intercede except for the one whom He approves of

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite at the grave of Imam Ali (AS) according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This supplication, transmitted through the chain of the Sixth Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, serves as a liturgical model for visiting the grave of Imam Ali, emphasizing his role as the primordial martyr (awwal mazlum) whose patience until death (al-yaqin) validates his intercessory authority. It integrates theological concepts of divine approval (artada) with the practical Shia practice of seeking mediation through the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the continuity of spiritual authority from the Prophet to the Imams.
